newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Millions of Bangladesh children given vaccinations.
newsitem.headline: Millions of Bangladesh children given vaccinations.

text.p: Health officials vaccinated millions of Bangladeshi children on Sunday in a continuing bid to stamp out polio, officials said. "We are determined to fight and eradicate polio by the year 2000," one official said.

Some 650,000 volunteers and health workers were aiming to administer vaccinations against the crippling disease at 120,000 health centres across the country to nearly 20 million children, the officials said.
Immunisation camps were also opened at ferry and bus terminals, and at railway stations, the officials said.

The preventive action, the third phase of a national vaccination drive, focused on children under five years old. Children under three years old are especially vulnerable to the illness which is largely spread by human excrement.

An earlier phase of vaccinations was completed in 1995 and another this year. The fourth and final dose of the orally-administered polio vaccine would be given to children on January 8, the officials said.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said on Saturday her government would launch a relentless effort to protect children from diseases and hunger.
She said a "formidable" number of Bangladeshi children became crippled every year due to polio attacks. But an exact estimate of children infected with polio was not available.

Bangladesh's vaccination programme was part of a global drive to wipe out poliomyelitis, an infectious viral disease that strikes the central nervous system and can cause temporary or permanent paralysis.
The disease thrives in hot and congested conditions common in the Indian sub-sontinent, according to the World Health Organisation.
